Reflection: gen 6 produced a decisive breakthrough. Applying the economically correct zero-R&D convention — unreported R&D means no knowledge capital — lifted the champion from 4.3% to **5.6% FF5 alpha, t=4.49, Sharpe 0.441 at 0.141 coverage**, i.e. better on every metric simultaneously and over the full valuation universe. That resolves the archive's main reliability caveat and tells us the mechanism is not confined to R&D reporters: the short leg needs the expensive non-innovators. Also useful from gen 6: dual scaling helped (4.1%, t=3.62), the built-not-bought composition worked (3.8%, t=3.56), the cash-flow leg again gave the best Sharpe (0.504), and earnings smoothing hurt. This generation therefore rebuilds the best refinements *on top of the full-universe convention*, and includes one attribution test that isolates how much of the new alpha comes from the R&D add-back in the value leg versus the knowledge-intensity leg.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: FullUniverse_DualScaled_Knowledge
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), MA(revt, 3)), RATIO(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Measuring hidden knowledge capital against both revenue and total assets removes scaler-specific distortions (thin margins on one side, asset-light business models on the other), so combining them within the full-universe convention should give the most stable ranking of intangible intensity and the most reliable alpha.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Dual scaling improved the R&D-reporter version (4.1% at t=3.62 versus 4.3% at t=3.83 for revenue alone, with the highest FMB slope of the two-leg family), and its benefit should be larger in the full universe where the zero-R&D mass makes the intangible ranking coarser. This is a measurement refinement of the leg we know matters, not an added channel of the type that diluted earlier stacks.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: FullUniverse_Knowledge_GrossProfitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), MA(revt, 3))), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap, knowledge-intensive firms deliver abnormal returns only when the underlying business earns gross profits; adding profitability across the full universe should raise cross-sectional precision by separating underpriced innovators from cash-burning shells and distressed non-innovators alike.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gross-profitability overlay produced the archive's strongest FMB slopes (6.6–7.0) while preserving 4.0% alpha in the narrow sample, and the full universe now contains many unprofitable non-R&D firms in the short leg that this screen will order more sensibly. If the FMB t-stat rises without sacrificing the 5.6% alpha, this becomes the best joint cross-sectional and portfolio evidence in the run.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: FullUniverse_CashPreferred_Knowledge
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ib), COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), MA(revt, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating cash flow plus R&D is the cleanest measure of the economic returns a buyer receives, and using reported earnings only when the cash flow statement is unavailable keeps that superior measure without sacrificing universe breadth.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cash-based value legs delivered the two highest Sharpe ratios in the archive (0.436 and 0.504) but always at roughly a third less coverage, so the fallback convention is exactly what is needed to combine measurement quality with breadth. This tests whether the full-universe alpha of 5.6% can be delivered with materially better risk-adjusted efficiency.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: FullUniverse_NetInternalIntangibleIntensity
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), COALESCE(gdwl, SUB(at, at))), MA(revt, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Only internally built intangibles are truly off the balance sheet; goodwill is already capitalized at an inflated price, so intangible intensity should be measured net of goodwill, penalizing serial acquirers and rewarding organic innovators within the same cheapness sort.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive repeatedly shows internal R&D earning positive alpha while goodwill-laden constructions earn negative alpha, and the bounded build-versus-buy share worked (3.8%, t=3.56) but cost coverage because it required `intan`; netting goodwill out of the same revenue-scaled intensity keeps full-universe coverage while sharpening the composition contrast. Both goodwill and R&D use the economically justified zero convention for non-reporters.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: FullUniverse_EBITDA_EV_Knowledge
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, COALESCE(xrd, SUB(at, at))), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), RATIO(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), MA(revt, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: EBITDA plus R&D measured against enterprise value strips out both intangible amortization and capital-structure effects, giving a cheapness measure that is undistorted for firms carrying purchased intangibles and for leveraged acquirers, which should improve the short leg of the interaction.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Earlier EV-based tests failed, but they were paired with the discredited `revt/intan` turnover leg rather than with knowledge intensity, so the valuation-metric question remains genuinely open within the winning frame. Because amortization of purchased intangibles depresses net income precisely for the acquirers we want to short, an amortization-free numerator could strengthen rather than dilute the spread.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: PlainYield_FullUniverse_KnowledgeTilt
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(COALESCE(TS_SUM(xrd, 5), SUB(at, at)), MA(revt, 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: If the interaction is driven by intangible intensity rather than by mechanically adding R&D back to earnings, an unadjusted earnings yield combined with full-universe knowledge intensity should retain most of the abnormal return.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: In the R&D-reporter sample the add-back was essential (dropping it took alpha from 2.3% to 0.0% when paired with intangible turnover), but that comparison used a leg we now know was uninformative, so the add-back's contribution to the 5.6% full-universe alpha is unmeasured. This attribution test determines whether the final recommended signal needs the R&D add-back at all, which matters for interpreting the mechanism as conservatism correction versus intangible-intensity tilt.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
